title: Probabilistic Traffic Scheduler for Model Experiments
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Create a lightweight A/B testing scheduler that allocates user traffic probabilistically across model versions and supports sequential early-stopping, shadow lanes, and automatic rollback. The goal is a product-safe experiment primitive that engineers and platform teams can launch from the Console with deterministic exposure guarantees, integrated statistical checks, and production-friendly observability. This ticket defines the experiment configuration, exposure caps, statistical tests, early-stop rules, rollback triggers, and Console UX hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Console: new experiment flow allowing selection of control and candidate model versions and probabilistic traffic schedule
Exposure controls: per-experiment global cap, per-customer cap, and minute-level burst limits implemented in routing layer
Statistical checks: sequential two-sided test with alpha spending (O'Brien-Fleming style) and multiple-comparisons correction when >2 variants
Early-stop rules: pre-configured thresholds for metric degradation (relative and absolute) and minimum sample thresholds enforced
Auto-rollback: automatic rollback pipeline that pins traffic back to baseline when safety gates trip and emits incident records
Shadow traffic: ability to mirror 100% of requests to candidate model without impact to response path and record divergence metrics
Observability: per-variant latency/cost/quality dashboards and automated alert thresholds exposed in Console
APIs: REST endpoints to create, update, pause, and stop experiments and to read experiment status and exposures
